messages:
devon: Heads-up — CI passed but our fused/paged attention perf regressed ~20-30% after yesterday's toolchain/container image bump. Repro on the dedicated perf harness and on my dev workstation when I switch to the same container image.

ci-bot: build/linux-gcc13-cuda12: all tests OK (unit/integration). Docker image: registry.redwood/inference/toolchain:2026-03-16-gcc13-bookworm

marta: Ugh. CI + green tests but perf down — that smells like ABI/toolchain changes affecting inlined kernels or codegen. Any perf numbers or flamegraphs?

devon: Quick numbers from perf harness (same commit, different toolchains):
```
# baseline toolchain (gcc12): avg tokens/sec = 810
# new toolchain (gcc13 image):  avg tokens/sec = 575
# ~29% regression
```
Also ran `perf stat` on the fused kernel binary: cycles up ~1.3x, cache-misses slightly higher. Attaching short perf top snapshot: lot of cycles spent in memcpy+memmove and __memcpy_wide_avx512 (we're on A100, so weird).

sam: Are these kernels being recompiled in CI or are we using prebuilt wheels? Could be different compiler flags or libstdc++ ABI.

devon: Our CI rebuilds kernels in the container at build time. I dug into the CI logs and found linker warnings that were previously ignored: 
```
ld: warning: libstdc++.so.6: version `CXXABI_1.4.1' not found (required by /opt/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so)
```
Not fatal, so CI stays green. But codegen changed: `-march=native` was removed from the Dockerfile in favor of a hermetic base image.

anya: Hmm, removing -march can definitely impact vectorized codegen. But would that explain memcpy-heavy profile? Maybe kernel chooser is falling back to a variant that does extra copies because it thinks some instructions are unsupported.

ryan: Also check batching heuristics. If the runtime sees different CPU feature flags it may change the kernel selection path (we check CPUID at runtime). The base image change could be masking features, so kernels choose generic path which copies into aligned buffers.

devon: Good call. I added an instrumented run that logs kernel selection decisions. For the failing runs the attention dispatcher picks: `fused_attention_generic_v2` instead of `fused_attention_avx2_blocked`. Log snippet: 
```
[attention] selected kernel fused_attention_generic_v2 (fallback) for seq_len=1024, batch=4
```
That generic path does extra linearization and memcopies.

marta: Do we have a regression test that asserts which kernel is chosen? We should.

sam: We don't; selection is heuristics-based with feature checks. Adding an assertion to the perf smoke (CI) that top kernel must be the optimized variant would catch this.

devon: Reproducer (run inside the problematic image):
```bash
# inside registry.redwood/inference/toolchain:2026-03-16-gcc13-bookworm
git checkout HEAD~0 -- path/to/fused_kernels
python -m perf_harness --model tiny --seq_len 1024 --batch 4 --profile -o out.pb
```
The harness prints chosen kernel and perf numbers.

anya: Another angle: glibc/gcc changes can alter inlining heuristics so code size thresholds differ -> different inlining -> different hot paths. Also libstdc++ ABI mismatch warnings suggest the container's libstdc++ is newer/older than expected; possible symbol versioning causing different impls of algo (string/mem routines).

devon: I also ran `nvprof`/nsys on the kernel and saw more memcpy calls at device-host boundary in the new image — suspicious because we didn't change device code. My current hypothesis: user-space copying because kernel variant expects packed KV layout but runtime produced different layout due to alignment rules changing with toolchain.

ryan: Can you paste the container's uname/gcc version and glibc?

devon: Sure: 
```
cat /etc/os-release -> Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm)
gcc --version -> gcc (Debian 13.1.0) 13.1.0
ldd --version -> glibc 2.36
```
Baseline CI image used earlier had gcc12 + glibc 2.35.

marta: Action items:
- pin CI image for fused attention perf pipelines (devon)
- add kernel-selection assertion to perf smoke (sam)
- add a tiny reproducer in tools/ so SRE can run image vs baseline (devon + ryan)
- infra: make the linker warnings fail build for perf-sensitive packages (marta)

sam: I'll send a small PR to the perf smoke that runs the harness with seq_len=1024, batch=4 and asserts chosen kernel contains "avx2" or "opt" in its name.

devon: I'll open a CI rollback PR that pins the toolchain image to the pre-bump hash and run a quick perf run. If that restores numbers we can be confident.

anya: Long term we should make the kernel chooser consider abi/toolchain flags and not rely solely on CPUID. Also add a runtime compatibility check that validates produced tensor layouts against kernel expectations (cheap checksum).

ryan: I'll take a look at the container Dockerfile for where -march got removed and see if we can re-enable targeted flags for the kernel build stage without hurting hermeticity.

ci-bot: Created ticket INF-1428: "perf: attention kernel regression after toolchain image bump" assigned to devon. :white_check_mark:

marta: Thanks. Please paste perf diffs and kernel-selection logs into the ticket. :eyes:

devon: Will do. Starting bisect/rollback now and I'll post results in INF-1428.

sam: Awesome — thanks for the clear reproducer. Once we have a patch we should add a tiny CI perf gate so future bumps don't slip by. :+1:

anya: Also let's add a short note in the release checklist about "verify kernel-selection in perf smoke" so product releases don't accidentally change toolchains without perf signoff.

devon: Agreed. Will update ticket with checklist items and assign follow-ups.

ryan: Ping me if you want help reproducing on a GPU host. I can spin up the exact A100 image locally.

devon: Thanks all. I'll update here when I have the bisect outcome.
